:::{#exm-convex-first-order}
#### Tangent lines under a parabola

For $f(x) = x^2$, the right side of @eq-supporting-hyperplane is
$y^2 + 2y (x - y) = 2xy - y^2$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x) - (2xy - y^2)
&= x^2 - 2xy + y^2 \\
&= (x - y)^2 \\
&\ge 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

with equality only at $x = y$, confirming that $x^2$ is strictly convex.
For $g(x) = -x^2$ the inequality fails:
at $y = 0$ the tangent line is $s = 0$, and $g(1) = -1 < 0$.

:::
